3.q: Trace the correct sequence linking an ancient Indian village tradition to its modern constitutional form.
3.a: The heritage chain runs: (1) Village elders gather (2) Panchayat consensus settles the dispute (3) The practice of community self-governance endures across centuries (4) The Constitution recognises grassroots democracy through local self-governance. A wrong answer that breaks this chain, such as crediting medieval foreign rulers with inventing village councils, shows the student cannot connect ancient Indian practices of community self-governance to the constitutional emphasis on grassroots democracy and local self-governance.

3.q: A district authority bans a peaceful citizens' meeting citing inconvenience. Which guarantee does this violate and what limit applies?
3.a: It violates the Right to Freedom, specifically the freedom of peaceful assembly under Article 19; the state may impose only reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order, so an arbitrary total ban infringes a Fundamental Right. A wrong answer that treats public spaces as fully at the government's disposal shows the student believes the state holds absolute control over assemblies, missing that Part III rights act as a shield against arbitrary state authority.
